trials.notes: Passed 8/8. Uses the correct WP_HTML_Processor fragment parser, finds the first H1, records depth, walks tokens until leaving the subtree, filters to #text tokens, and reads decoded text with get_modifiable_text(). All called HTML API methods are documented in the rendered files.

Passed 8/8. Same documented processor/token-walk pattern as the reference. The extra class_exists() guard is ordinary PHP, not hallucinated HTML API usage, and did not cause misuse or _doing_it_wrong records.

Passed 8/8. Reference-equivalent implementation using documented create_fragment(), next_tag(), get_current_depth(), next_token(), get_token_type(), and get_modifiable_text(). Correctly handles decoded entities, nested markup, empty heading text, and unclosed input.

failure_analysis: No failed hidden case appeared in any trial: all three passed all 8 frozen cases and execution.json showed no _doing_it_wrong or trigger_error records. The rendered docs did well on this task. html-processor.md has a dedicated text-extraction section that says ordinary subtree text should be collected from #text tokens reached by an HTML Processor subtree walk, not by calling get_modifiable_text() on every token. The next_token() heading explains that text may be split across tokens, that the walk must be bounded because next_token() otherwise continues to the end, and that special elements carry text differently. The get_current_depth() heading explains the >= depth boundary, and get_modifiable_text() states that #text output is already decoded UTF-8. create_fragment() also makes the body-fragment parser choice clear. The only near-miss is that this task was almost exactly covered by the LI/article text examples, so these successes do not prove the docs would prevent mistakes in less directly mirrored text-content tasks.

doc_gaps.problem: The base method explains that comments, processing instructions, SCRIPT/STYLE, TEXTAREA/TITLE, and #text can all have modifiable text, but the strongest 'not a predicate for ordinary DOM text' warning is clearer on the HTML Processor override and surrounding guide prose.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an explicit warning and @see from the base docblock: for ordinary DOM-style text extraction, first require get_token_type() === '#text' and prefer WP_HTML_Processor subtree walks for parsed body fragments.

doc_gaps.problem: The current examples are strong, but the general contract is embedded in examples for specific elements such as LI and UL. Users may still miss that the pattern applies to any matched container and that an empty container should yield an empty accumulated string.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general contract paragraph: after matching any opener, record its current depth, walk next_token() while depth is at least that opener depth, append only #text get_modifiable_text(), and treat no visited #text tokens as an empty text result rather than absence of the element.

doc_gaps.problem: The body-fragment factory behavior is documented, but the decision between create_fragment(), create_full_parser(), and new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor() is spread across guide prose and method docs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact chooser note near the factory: use create_fragment($html) for markup that lives inside BODY, create_full_parser() for complete documents or HEAD content, and Tag Processor for lexical token edits where tree-aware text content is not required.
